name: v0.6.11: Firecracker from install.sh, and Stop/Start that works and stays small
body:
## Features in v0.6.11

This release is about Firecracker. `install.sh --with-firecracker` sets a server up for Firecracker sandboxes, the way `--with-gvisor` does for gVisor. A stopped Firecracker sandbox can be started again on servers that run the jailer, which is every production server. And Stop and Start now copy only a sandbox's data, so a stopped sandbox takes about as much disk as it holds, not its full disk size.

> **Stopped Firecracker sandboxes could not be started on earlier releases.** Start failed with `Permission denied (os error 13) rootfs.ext4` on every server that runs the jailer. v0.6.11 fixes Start; the saved format is unchanged, so sandboxes stopped on an earlier release can be started after the upgrade.

### Highlights

- **`install.sh --with-firecracker`.** The installer checks that the server has `/dev/kvm` before it installs anything, then installs Firecracker and its jailer v1.15.1 and guest kernel 5.10.245. Every download is checked against a SHA-256 written into the script. Virtual machines run as a new `sandboxd-jailer` system user. Running it again downloads nothing that is already installed.
- **Stopped Firecracker sandboxes start again.** The restored disk is now handed to the VM's user before the VM opens it.
- **Stop and Start keep disks small and are faster.** Copies skip empty space. On an AWS `m5zn.metal`, a sandbox with a 10 GiB disk and 1 GiB of memory that wrote 256 MiB: the saved copy went from 11,265 MiB to 597 MiB, Stop from 108 s to 15 s, and Start from 88 s to 3.6 s.

---

### Installer (#903)

- `--with-firecracker` refuses a server without `/dev/kvm`, a non-Linux server or an architecture other than x86_64 and aarch64, before installing anything, and says what to change. It does not work with `--local` or `--cli-only`.
- Versions are the ones Terraform and Ansible install. The kernel bucket publishes no checksums, so the SHA-256 of the release tarball, the kernel and its config, for both architectures, are written into the script.
- A kernel already at `/var/lib/sandboxd/firecracker/vmlinux` is kept. Its config must set `CONFIG_VMGENID=y`, or the installer stops.
- It also installs `skopeo`, `umoci`, `e2fsprogs` and `iproute2`, and writes `SB_ENABLE_FIRECRACKER=true` and the jailer user's `SB_JAILER_UID` and `SB_JAILER_GID`. All paths are the server's defaults.
- The installer options page shows every command for turning Firecracker on, with `sudo` where it is needed.
- Live: installed and ran a Firecracker sandbox on `m5zn.metal` (x86_64) and `c7g.metal` (aarch64).

### Firecracker Stop and Start (#904, #905)

- **Start.** Firecracker reopens a VM's disks as the jailer's user while it loads the snapshot. The restored disk was given to that user only after the load. It is now given before, on Start and on a create from a template whose templates folder is on a different filesystem.
- **Copies.** Stop copies the disk and memory out of the VM's jail and Start copies the disk back. A plain copy wrote every empty byte, so each copy took the full disk size. Copies now ask the filesystem where the data is, read only that, and skip every 4 KiB block of zeros. The copy holds the same bytes, so the snapshot checksum check and the restored VM see no difference. The memory file shrinks too, because unused memory is zeros: 1,024 MiB to 317 MiB in the run above.
- Live, same run: server disk used while the restarted sandbox runs went from 21,507 MiB to 880 MiB, and the sandbox's data matched after every Start.

### Dependencies (#787)

- `github.com/mdlayher/netlink` 1.11.2.

### Upgrade notes

- **Saved copies made by earlier releases stay full-size** until the sandbox's next Stop rewrites them.
- **Pass `--with-firecracker` on every later run of the installer.** Each run rewrites `/etc/sandboxd/sandboxd.env`, so a run without it turns Firecracker off.
- **Terraform and Ansible servers are unchanged.** They install Firecracker their own way and run the jailer as uid 1000.

name: v0.6.10: Key custody enforced, and safe create retries
body:
## Features in v0.6.10

This release finishes the work v0.6.9 started. Enterprise servers that use your own key store now refuse to run with a plain server key. A create retried while the first attempt is still running gets the same sandbox. The last two plain hashes over request bodies that can hold secrets are now keyed with the server key. The SDKs, published as 0.8.0 alongside this release, send a retry-safe key on every create and expose the server's error code.

> **Enterprise servers with a key store must wrap the server key before they upgrade.** With `SB_ENTERPRISE_MODE=true` and `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER` set to `vault`, `pkcs11` or `awskms`, v0.6.10 refuses to start while `SB_CREDENTIAL_KEY_CUSTODY` is still `file`. v0.6.9 warned about this at start and with the `SandboxdServerKeyPlaintext` alert. Wrap the key on v0.6.9 first (see the upgrade notes).

### Highlights

- **A key store means a wrapped server key.** An enterprise server with a customer key store will not start while its server key is a plain file. `sandboxd key` still runs on such a server, so `sandboxd key wrap` is always available to fix it.
- **Retrying a create is safe, even while the first attempt runs.** A v1 or Daytona create retried with the same `Idempotency-Key` and the same request now waits for the create already running and returns its sandbox. Before, the retry started a second create of the same sandbox, and when that failed it could take away the first create's capacity reservation and mounts.
- **The SDKs send a key on every create.** Each SDK generates an `Idempotency-Key` once per create call and sends the same key on its own automatic retries, so a create retried after a timeout or a dropped connection no longer makes a second sandbox. Pass your own key to make your own retries of the whole call safe too.
- **Every SDK exposes the server's error code.** TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust and Java errors carry the HTTP status, the server's `code` (such as `idempotency_key_reused` or `overloaded`) and the `Retry-After` wait.
- **No plain hashes over secret-bearing bodies are left.** The Runloop devbox ID and the exec audit record's digest are now HMACs under a key derived from the server key, like the E2B fingerprint in v0.6.9. A guessed env value can no longer be checked offline against either.

---

### Key custody (#813)

- With `SB_ENTERPRISE_MODE=true` and an external `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER` (`vault`, `pkcs11` or `awskms`), the server refuses to start unless `SB_CREDENTIAL_KEY_CUSTODY=wrapped`. The error names the fix: run `sandboxd key wrap`, set `SB_CREDENTIAL_KEY_CUSTODY=wrapped` and delete the plaintext key.
- `sandboxd key` loads the same configuration without this check, so a refused server can still be wrapped in place.
- The `SandboxdServerKeyPlaintext` alert now fires only on enterprise servers with no key store, and tells the operator to move the key to one.
- The enterprise and KMS integration scenarios are built with `key_custody = "wrapped"`.
- Live: the enterprise boot-gate matrix, a KMS-wrapped cluster from the start, and a disabled KMS key passed on a 3-node enterprise cluster.

### Create retries (#900)

- One create of a sandbox ID runs on a server at a time. A create that finds another create of the same ID running waits for it, then sees what a retry arriving a moment later would see: the finished sandbox, which it returns, or nothing if the first create failed, in which case it creates afresh.
- A keyed create with a different request is still refused at once with `422 idempotency_key_reused`.
- The wait is bounded by the client's own request and by the create timeout plus its rollback. Past that, the retry gets `503 create_in_progress` with `Retry-After: 5`, and nothing was changed.
- A failed create no longer releases or undoes state it does not own: the capacity reservation, the external mounts, the public route, and the Daytona, E2B and Runloop facade records of a sandbox that a retry replayed.
- **Cluster.** A keyed retry whose create is still being placed is sent to the node that holds the reservation and waits there, instead of answering `503` or `409`. The incarnation conflict between nodes now travels as `409` with its meaning intact. A target that refuses a keyed create gives back its reservation instead of holding the sandbox name for two minutes.
- Live: 16 and 32 concurrent creates with one key, sent through every ingress node of a 3-node cluster, made one sandbox and one capacity reservation (UC-367). Also passed on a cluster with a separate ingress, a bare-metal Firecracker server and a V8-isolate server.

### Keyed digests (#897)

- **Runloop devbox ID.** Still `sb-` and 16 hex characters, now cut from an HMAC over the caller's account, the `x-request-id` and the body. A retry still finds its devbox on the same server through a server-key rotation, and for 4 minutes after an upgrade it also finds a devbox made under the old ID. With no usable server key, a create that carries an `x-request-id` is refused with `503`.
- **Exec audit digest.** With the default `SB_AUDIT_EXEC_COMMAND=digest`, an exec's audit record now holds `hmac:<key id>:<hex>` instead of a 64-character SHA-256. Identical requests still give identical digests until the server key is rotated. Records already written keep their old digests, and the audit chain verifies with both kinds. A server with no usable key records the call with no digest, never a plain hash.
- Live: a Runloop create retried through a second node got the same devbox, and one exec body got the same digest on two nodes (UC-366).

### SDKs 0.8.0 (#898, #899)

- **Error types.** TypeScript `MicroVMApiError` (`status`, `code`, `retryAfterMs`), Python `MicroVMHTTPError` now importable from `microvm` (`status_code`, `code`, `retry_after`), Go `*APIError` (`StatusCode`, `Code`, `RetryAfter`), Rust `Error::Api(ApiError)` (`status()`, `code()`, `message()`, `retry_after()`), Java `MicroVMApiException` (`getStatusCode()`, `getCode()`, `getRetryAfter()`). Messages and retry behavior are unchanged.
- **Idempotency-Key.** Every SDK's sandbox create sends one: yours if you pass it (`idempotencyKey` in TypeScript and Java, `idempotency_key` in Python and Rust, `CreateWithIdempotencyKey` in Go), otherwise 128 random bits generated once per call and reused on that call's retries. Only sandbox create sends it.
- The `aerolvm` CLI, the MCP tools and the server's remote MCP endpoint use the Go SDK, so their creates send a key too.

### Upgrade notes

- **Enterprise servers with a key store: wrap first.** On v0.6.9, run `sandboxd key wrap` on one server, copy `credential_encryption.key.wrapped` to every server, set `SB_CREDENTIAL_KEY_CUSTODY=wrapped`, remove `SB_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` from the env files, run `sandboxd key verify`, delete the old key file, and restart one server at a time. Then upgrade. A server upgraded first refuses to start, and `sandboxd key wrap` still works on it. Terraform users set `key_custody = "wrapped"`. Servers without enterprise mode, or without a key store, are unaffected.
- **New answers on create.**

  | Status | Code | `Retry-After` | When |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 503 | `create_in_progress` | 5 | A keyed retry waited the whole create timeout for the create it repeats. Nothing was changed. |
  | 503 | none | 1 | In a cluster, a keyed retry whose create settled while the retry was being routed, or whose reservation is gone. Was a `409` in one case. |

- **Exec audit digests change format.** Anything that reads the `digest` field of exec audit records, such as a SIEM rule, must accept `hmac:<key id>:<hex>` as well as the old 64-character hex. Digests change again when the server key is rotated.
- **Runloop devbox IDs change for new creates.** Existing devboxes keep their IDs. A Runloop create retried across nodes while they disagree on the current server key (during a rotation) or run different releases (during a rolling upgrade) can still make a second devbox.
- **SDK 0.8.0 is a breaking release for Rust.** HTTP errors are `Error::Api(ApiError)` instead of `Error::Api(String)`, and the SDK's own errors moved to a new `Error::Client(String)`. `Error` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a `match` on it needs a `_` arm. `CreateOptions` gains `idempotency_key`, so a struct literal without `..Default::default()` must add it. The other SDKs only add to their APIs.
- **Every SDK create is now a keyed create.** On the server, each one costs one HMAC at the API edge, one extra database read and one small row (`sandbox_create_digests`), a few microseconds in all.
- **Rolling upgrades.** Old and new servers work together in a cluster. The incarnation conflict travels as `409` only between upgraded nodes; an older node still sees a `500` and answers that create's retry with a `503` the SDKs retry.

name: v0.6.9: Your own key store, and sandboxes fenced off by default
body:
## Features in v0.6.9

This release has two parts. Customer key custody lets you keep the key that protects sandbox secrets in your own key store. The rest comes from a bank-readiness review: a live test campaign on AWS that tried to break sandbox isolation, use up a server's resources and overload the API, on every runtime. The fixes from that review are in this release, and the tests that found the problems are now part of the integration suite.

> **Stricter defaults. Read the upgrade notes before you upgrade.** Sandboxes can no longer reach the server they run on, other sandboxes on the same server, the cloud metadata service, or anything over IPv6. Firecracker templates built by an older release must be deleted and re-created. The Terraform module now requires `admin_allowed_cidrs`.

### Highlights

- **Keep the server key in your own key store.** Vault or OpenBao Transit, an HSM over PKCS#11, or AWS KMS can now hold the key that protects sandbox secrets. Each server keeps only a wrapped copy and unlocks it into memory when it starts. Revoke the key in your key store and every server that can reach it stops using your data within about 15 minutes, with no restart. Restore the key and they resume. The new `sandboxd key` command checks, wraps and rotates the server key. It is off until you turn it on.
- **Sandboxes are fenced off by default.** A sandbox cannot reach the cloud metadata service, the services on its own server, other sandboxes on the same server, or anything over IPv6. A server that cannot put one of these fences in place refuses new sandboxes with a `503` the SDKs retry, instead of running them without it.
- **The agent inside a Firecracker sandbox needs that sandbox's token.** Sandboxes started from a template or the warm pool used to run it with no token at all. Firecracker sandboxes also get the `env` they were created with now. Before, they ignored it.
- **Limits on what one sandbox can use.** Container sandboxes get a process limit (4,096 by default). A sandbox that writes past its disk size is stopped. A process killed for running out of memory no longer stops its sandbox or removes its network rules.
- **Busy servers say "retry later" instead of falling over.** In a cluster, each node runs at most 16 cluster-wide sandbox lists at once and shares them fairly between teams. The rest get `503 overloaded` or `429 rate_limited`, with `Retry-After: 1`. The health watchdog restarts only a server that has stopped answering, never a busy one. A node whose network slots are full answers `503` with `Retry-After: 30`, and the cluster places the create on another node.
- **All five SDKs wait as long as `Retry-After` asks.** A retry after a 429 or 503 waits for the server's hint, up to 30 seconds per retry by default. SDKs are published separately from the server.
- **Fewer copies of your secrets.** A Docker snapshot no longer keeps the sandbox's internal token or the `env` it was created with. The E2B create fingerprint, which was a plain hash that included `env` values, is now keyed with the server key.
- **A reused `Idempotency-Key` must come with the same create.** A v1 or Daytona create that reuses an `Idempotency-Key` with a different request now gets `422 idempotency_key_reused` instead of the first request's sandbox. A retry of the same request still returns the first sandbox.

---

### Customer key custody (#784, #801–#823)

- **New key stores.** `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER` gains `vault` (HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao, Transit engine) and `pkcs11` (an HSM). The HSM vendor's library runs in a supervised helper process, never inside sandboxd. AWS KMS (`awskms`) now reports a disabled or deleted key as revoked.
- **Wrapped server key.** With `SB_CREDENTIAL_KEY_CUSTODY=wrapped`, the server key is on disk only as `credential_encryption.key.wrapped`. The key file, the environment, `cluster.env`, the cluster credential bundle and its S3 copy no longer hold it in plain form. A server refuses to start while a plain copy is still around. `install.sh --key-custody wrapped`, `cluster-init.sh --key-custody wrapped` and the Terraform `key_custody` variable set it up. The Terraform variable uses the module's AWS KMS key.
- **Revoke.** With wrapped custody, each server unwraps its key file again every `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER_RECHECK_INTERVAL` (5 minutes). After `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER_REVOKE_AFTER` (3) "revoked" answers in a row, the key leaves memory. Creating, starting or restoring sandboxes, running commands, reading files and opening SSH then get `503 key_revoked`. SSH sessions and toolbox streams close. The egress gateway drops its inspection CA and injected secrets, and `/health` reports `key_custody: "revoked"`. An outage or a permission error never counts. The first good answer brings the server back. Each step is written to the audit log.
- **Rotation.** After you rotate the key in your key store, each server moves its stored secrets onto the new version in the background, once an hour. `aerolvm_key_rows_stale` at 0 on every server means the old version can be retired. The server key itself rotates with `sandboxd key rotate --stage`, `--promote` and `--retire`, with either custody. Once the old key is retired, a copy of it opens nothing in the current database.
- **`sandboxd key`.** `status`, `verify`, `wrap`, `rewrap`, `unwrap`, `ack-migration` and `rotate`. `sandboxd key status --check` lists where every key lives.
- **Key-store errors are clear.** They answer `503` with a stable code (`key_revoked`, `key_version_retired`, `key_store_denied`, `key_store_throttled`, `key_store_unavailable`) and fixed text. The key store's own reply never reaches a client, and Vault's error text stays out of the logs. Each server runs at most `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER_MAX_INFLIGHT` (8) key-store calls at once.
- **Operations.** Four alerts in the `sandboxd.key-custody` group, a Key custody row on the security dashboard, metrics for every key-store call, and a key-custody section in the secrets runbook.
- **Enterprise mode.** `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER_STRICT_BOOT=true` is required for every key store, and a PKCS#11 software token is refused. A plain server key next to a key store logs a warning at start. This release warns. It does not refuse.
- **Tested.** CI runs the Vault checks against Vault 1.18 and OpenBao 2.1. Live AWS scenarios with OpenBao, a software HSM and AWS KMS passed from fresh clusters, and a run on AWS CloudHSM passed on real hardware.

### Sandbox isolation (#824, #826, #838, #839, #845, #848, #851, #855, #888)

- **Cloud metadata is never reachable.** That covers `169.254.169.254` (AWS, GCP, Azure, OpenStack, Oracle, DigitalOcean), the AWS ECS and EKS credential endpoints, Azure WireServer, Alibaba Cloud metadata, and AWS's IPv6 forms. They are dropped on every server, with or without an operator egress file, and a sandbox's own allowlist cannot open them. The Terraform module sets the node metadata hop limit to 1.
- **The server is closed to its sandboxes.** A sandbox can reach only a short list on its own server: the egress gateway's DNS and proxy ports, DNS on a server address when the sandbox's resolver points there, and ports 80 and 443 on a server that serves public URLs. WASM and isolate sandboxes get the same check. `SB_SANDBOX_NODE_PORTS_ALLOW` adds ports (not allowed in enterprise mode). The host-port redirect listener used by ingress proxy routing is guarded too.
- **Sandboxes on one server cannot reach each other.** That includes sandboxes of different runtimes, such as a Firecracker guest and a container. Each runtime's subnet now has its own deny-floor chain, so a server running several runtimes keeps all of them. `SB_SANDBOX_INTERCONNECT=true` restores the old behavior (not allowed in enterprise mode).
- **No IPv6 in sandboxes.** IPv6 is off inside every container, gVisor and Firecracker sandbox, and the server drops IPv6 on every sandbox network.
- **Fail closed.** While the server guard, the IPv6 fence or the metadata deny floor is not in place, new container, gVisor and Firecracker sandboxes on that runtime are refused with `503` and `Retry-After: 5` (`node_guard_not_ready`, `ipv6_fence_not_ready`, `egress_floor_not_ready`). The deny floor is checked every 30 seconds and put back if a firewall reload removed it. `aerolvm_egress_floor_ready` shows its state. Local mode, where the host firewall is off, is unchanged outside enterprise mode.
- **Network policy that cannot be enforced is refused.** On a server with the host firewall off (`install.sh --local`, or `SB_ENABLE_NETWORK_RULES=false`), a request for block-all, an address list, hostname rules or a byte cap gets `501 network_policy_unenforced`. Before, it was accepted and nothing was blocked. WASM and isolate sandboxes filter their own traffic and are unaffected.
- **Firecracker.** The agent in the VM answers nothing but `/health` until the server hands it the sandbox's token over the VM's private channel, on every boot path. Firecracker guests are fenced off from each other and from new inbound connections. The `env` a sandbox was created with reaches every command, terminal and SSH session in the VM, as it does in a container. It is never written to the VM's disk, and a VM that cannot take it fails the create.
- **Docker.** A restricted create on the Docker engine without a pool slot starts its own pause container, so the sandbox's network rules are on before its program runs.
- **Known limits.** gVisor on the Docker engine still gets its network rules a moment after its program starts. On containerd, the default server engine, there is no gap.

### Limits per sandbox (#826, #827, #859, #862)

- **Process limit.** `SB_SANDBOX_PIDS_LIMIT` (default 4,096) applies to Docker and containerd sandboxes and warm slots. A gVisor sandbox gets the limit inside gVisor, lowered to one process per MiB of memory (1,024 for a 1 GiB sandbox), so a fork bomb fails inside it instead of crashing it. A self-copying fork bomb can still end a gVisor sandbox. It harms only that sandbox.
- **Disk.** Every `SB_DISK_LIMIT_CHECK_INTERVAL` (15 seconds), a container sandbox that has written more than its disk size plus 5% is stopped. Its data is kept, the reason is in `last_error`, and the stop is audited as `lifecycle.disk_limit_stop`. Firecracker, WASM and isolate sandboxes are not checked.
- **Out of memory.** A process killed for running out of memory is recorded and counted (`aerolvm_sandbox_oom_events_total`). The sandbox stops only when it actually exits, and then the stop is recorded as an out-of-memory kill. Before, the sandbox was marked stopped while it kept running, and its network restrictions were removed.

### Overload and capacity (#830, #852, #880, #881, #882, #886, #889)

- **Watchdog.** sandboxd answers a liveness probe on its own socket (`SB_LIVENESS_SOCKET`) that load cannot slow down. The `install.sh` watchdog restarts sandboxd only after 3 failed probes in a row over at least 90 seconds, never in its first 120 seconds, and never while a start or stop is under way.
- **List gate.** Each cluster node runs at most `SB_API_LIST_MAX_INFLIGHT` (16) cluster-wide lists at once, for v1 and the Daytona, E2B and Runloop facades. A list waits up to `SB_API_LIST_QUEUE_WAIT` (500 ms) for a slot, then gets `503 overloaded`. Identical placement reads made at the same moment share one control-plane request. A single server is never gated.
- **Fair share.** A team or account may hold at most `SB_API_LIST_MAX_INFLIGHT_PER_TENANT` slots (a quarter of the gate, 4 by default). Waiting tenants take turns. A tenant over its share gets `429 rate_limited`, and the others keep working. The share follows the team or account, never the token, so minting more tokens buys no more share.
- **Measured.** At 1,024 list clients, the cluster went from 70 successful lists a second, a 37-second p99 and 5,081 `502` errors to 2,084 lists a second, a 950 ms p99 and no errors. The two runs used different clusters, and the `503` path was not reached in the live run.
- **Network slots count as capacity.** A full containerd network-namespace pool, Firecracker TAP pool or Docker bridge now answers `503` with `Retry-After: 30`, like running out of CPU or memory. Before, it answered `400` or `500`. Each worker reports these pools under `slot_pools` on `GET /v1/capacity`, and placement skips a node whose pool is full. An isolate create that needs an egress slot in a full tenant group gets the same `503`, instead of starting with its network silently denied.
- **Docker bridge.** A Linux bridge holds 1,023 ports. A Docker-engine worker now counts its sandbox bridge as a slot pool: 1,000 on a stock `docker0`, or `SB_DOCKER_BRIDGE_SLOTS`.
- **Leader changes.** A cluster write that finds the leader gone answers `503` with `Retry-After: 2`. Before, it answered `400` with an internal address in the message.
- **Restarts.** A cluster node that has just restarted answers `503` with `Retry-After: 1` for a sandbox it cannot see yet, instead of a false `404`. It keeps serving the sandboxes it holds.

### SDKs (#884)

- A 429 or 503 retry waits for `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP date), never less than the SDK's own backoff, plus up to 20% random spread, capped per retry. The cap is `maxRetryAfterMs` in TypeScript, Python and Java, `MaxRetryAfterMs` in Go and `max_retry_after_ms` in Rust: 30,000 by default, and `0` ignores `Retry-After`. Which calls retry, how often, and on which answers is unchanged.
- TypeScript adds a `signal` client option. Aborting it ends the request and any retry wait.
- Docs: "When the server is busy" in SDK setup.

### Secrets (#891, #892)

- **Docker snapshots.** The saved image keeps the sandbox's files. Every variable the create added, and the server's internal token for the sandbox, are cleared. Docker cannot remove a variable from a saved image, so the names stay with empty values. A sandbox started from the snapshot gets only the `env` of its own create. A pushed snapshot carries none of the values. Docker's classic image store still keeps a hidden parent image with the original settings on the node until the snapshot is deleted.
- **E2B create fingerprint.** The fingerprint that lets a retried E2B create return the same sandbox used to be a plain hash of the request, `env` values included, and part of it became the sandbox ID. It is now an HMAC under a key derived from the server key. Retries still return the same sandbox on any node and across restarts.

### Fixes

- **Exec.** A command whose sandbox dies now fails within seconds with `409` "sandbox is not running" on Docker, containerd and gVisor, and within 30 seconds on Firecracker. Before, it waited about three minutes for a `502`. A command that runs a long time with no output is never cut off (#856).
- **containerd.** A sandbox no longer freezes after printing about 128 KiB of output, and output is read again after a sandboxd restart (#872). Warm-pool sandboxes start again after a stop (#871). Network slots no longer leak their address leases and NAT rules, which piled up worst on gVisor (#834). A restored warm slot that holds another address is rebuilt (#868).
- **Firecracker.** Calls into a sandbox no longer fail with `502 connection reset` when a new sandbox reuses an old one's address (#825).
- **gVisor.** An exec under load no longer loses its exit code and reports `-1` (#829).
- **Reconcile.** A sandbox is deleted only when its runtime says it is gone. One the runtime cannot answer for is left alone and, after 10 minutes, marked `error` with a `runtime state unknown:` message. Before, a healthy gVisor sandbox could be deleted (#836).
- **Network rules.** On the Docker engine, removing a pause container also clears the firewall rules on its address, so the next sandbox there inherits none (#867). A hostname-filtered create hands off to the egress gateway while the sandbox builds, and its temporary block is lifted with one nftables set add (#850, #854, #863, #869).
- **Mounts.** The cleanup sweep no longer kills an S3 mount that is still starting. A mount whose tool exits fails at once with the real reason. A node without the mount program answers `501 mount_tool_unavailable` instead of `400` (#860).
- **Cluster.** A create that names a snapshot's image works from any node (#831). In a cluster, an SSH session is recorded on the sandbox's own server, and the calls that carry it name the sandbox key, not the operator (#833). The JS-bundle and template lists are no longer marked partial on a cluster whose leader does not run that runtime (#835). Draining every backup of an HA sandbox's secret no longer leaves its reseal stuck (#843).
- **Audit.** After a burst of refused credentials from one address, the count of the rest is written within about 70 seconds, even if the address goes quiet (#844).
- **Dashboard.** Sign-in asks for the `groups` scope when the provider offers it, so group rules work with Dex (#782).
- **CLI.** `aerolvm audit verify`, `audit search` and `access review` download S3 export files in parallel (`--fetch-concurrency`, default 32). Ctrl-C now stops cleanly (#832).

### Install, Terraform and operations (#812, #817, #818, #823, #828, #857, #864, #870, #880)

- **Watchdog.** The `install.sh` watchdog also starts a `sandboxd.service` that systemd gave up on, once the cause is gone. A unit you stopped yourself is left alone.
- **Backups.** `sandboxd-backup.sh` carries the server key files: the wrapped file with wrapped custody, otherwise `credential_encryption.key` and the key ring. `sandboxd-restore.sh` moves the replacement node's own database, Raft log and key files aside before it restores.
- **Joining servers.** A Terraform joiner is installed with the new `install.sh --no-start`, so it never makes a server key of its own before it joins.
- **Terraform admin access.** `admin_allowed_cidrs` has no default, and a `/0` range is refused unless `allow_admin_from_anywhere = true`. The API stays open inside the VPC.
- **Load balancer.** `api_load_balancer = "nlb"` puts a health-checked AWS Network Load Balancer in front of the ingress nodes. Raw TCP ports then move to `tcp.<domain>` (`SB_L4_PUBLIC_HOST`). The default, `"none"`, changes nothing.
- **rpcbind.** `install.sh` turns rpcbind off after installing the NFS client, unless it was already on. Linux `--local` installs now get the mount tools.
- **Ingress proxy routing.** The route responder also listens on the `aerolvm-rt` link's own address (`SB_ROUTE_DNS_LINK_ADDR`), which stops 20-second resolver stalls that dropped new connections.

### New docs

- Use your own key store (#809).
- SSO: each identity provider is listed in the Enterprise sidebar, with setup notes for Dex (#783).
- Blog: Staying up under overload; Keeping sandboxes away from the node's cloud credentials; How the in-sandbox agent knows who is calling; The life of an API key in AerolVM (#883, #885, #887).

### Dependencies

- Go 1.26.10, for GO-2026-6809 (#816).
- `github.com/klauspost/compress` 1.20.3, for GHSA-fpmh-frq8-7rj8 (#800).

### Upgrade notes

- **Key custody changes nothing until you turn it on.** The defaults are `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER=local` and `SB_CREDENTIAL_KEY_CUSTODY=file`, and a server with them contacts no key store. To wrap an existing server key: run `sandboxd key wrap` on one server, copy `credential_encryption.key.wrapped` to every server, set `SB_CREDENTIAL_KEY_CUSTODY=wrapped`, remove `SB_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` from the env files, run `sandboxd key verify`, delete the old key file, and restart one server at a time. Backups made before the wrap still hold the plain key until you destroy them or rotate the server key.
- **Server-key rotation is one-way.** Every server must run v0.6.9 before `sandboxd key rotate --stage`, which checks this. After `--stage` the wrapped key file uses a format older releases cannot read, and after `--promote` no server can go back to an older release.
- **AWS KMS users.** Key-store failures now answer `503` with a code (see the table below) instead of `400` or `500`. At most `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER_MAX_INFLIGHT` (8) key-store calls run at once per server; past that, calls back off and then fail with `503 key_store_throttled`.
- **Enterprise mode.** The new `SandboxdServerKeyPlaintext` alert (warning) fires on an enterprise server whose server key is not wrapped. This release only warns.
- **New and changed responses.** SDKs retry the `503` and `429` answers by default. They do not retry `501` or `422`.

  | Status | Code | `Retry-After` | When |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 503 | `overloaded` | 1 | A cluster-wide list (v1, Daytona, E2B, Runloop) finds the node's list slots full. Cluster mode only. |
  | 429 | `rate_limited` | 1 | The caller's team or account already holds its share of the node's list slots. Cluster mode only. |
  | 503 | none | 30 | The node's network slots or Docker bridge are full. Was `400` or `500`. |
  | 503 | `node_guard_not_ready`, `ipv6_fence_not_ready`, `egress_floor_not_ready` | 5 | A container, gVisor or Firecracker create while the server's guard, IPv6 fence or metadata deny floor is not in place. |
  | 503 | none | 2 | A cluster write while the leader changes. Was `400`. |
  | 503 | none | 1 | A restarted cluster node has not caught up and cannot see the sandbox yet. Was `404`. |
  | 503 | `key_store_throttled` / `key_store_unavailable` | 1 / 5 | The key store is throttling or cannot be reached. |
  | 503 | `key_revoked`, `key_version_retired`, `key_store_denied` | none | The key store revoked the key, retired its version, or refused this server. |
  | 501 | `network_policy_unenforced` | none | A network policy on a server with the host firewall off. Was accepted and not enforced. |
  | 501 | `mount_tool_unavailable` | none | The node lacks the mount program. Was `400`. |
  | 501 | none | none | A Firecracker create from a template built by an older release, or a start of a Firecracker sandbox stopped before the upgrade. |
  | 409 | none | none | An exec, file call or session whose sandbox stopped while it ran. Was a `502` after minutes. The E2B facade keeps its `502`. |
  | 422 | `idempotency_key_reused` | none | A v1 or Daytona create reuses an `Idempotency-Key` with a different request. |

- **New settings.** All are optional. `setup/config-defaults.md` has the details.

  | Setting | Default |
  |---|---|
  | `SB_API_LIST_MAX_INFLIGHT` | `16` (`0` turns the gate off) |
  | `SB_API_LIST_MAX_INFLIGHT_PER_TENANT` | a quarter of the gate, at least 1 (`4`) |
  | `SB_API_LIST_QUEUE_WAIT` | `500ms` |
  | `SB_LIVENESS_SOCKET` | `/run/sandboxd/live.sock` (`off` disables it) |
  | `SB_SANDBOX_INTERCONNECT` | `false` |
  | `SB_SANDBOX_NODE_PORTS_ALLOW` | empty |
  | `SB_SANDBOX_PIDS_LIMIT` | `4096` (`0` = unlimited) |
  | `SB_DISK_LIMIT_CHECK_INTERVAL` | `15s` (`0` = off) |
  | `SB_ALLOW_UNENFORCED_NETWORK_POLICY` | `false` |
  | `SB_TOOLBOX_DEAD_PEER_TIMEOUT` | `30s` (`0` = off) |
  | `SB_DOCKER_BRIDGE_SLOTS` | `0`, sized at start (1,000 on a stock `docker0`) |
  | `SB_L4_PUBLIC_HOST` | empty |
  | `SB_ROUTE_DNS_LINK_ADDR` | empty (`install.sh --ingress-proxy-routing` sets `169.254.53.53:53053`) |
  | `SB_CREDENTIAL_KEY_CUSTODY` | `file` |
  | `SB_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY_WRAPPED_PATH` | `/var/lib/sandboxd/credential_encryption.key.wrapped` |
  | `SB_CREDENTIAL_KEY_RING_PATH` | the key file path plus `.ring` |
  | `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER_MAX_INFLIGHT` | `8` |
  | `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER_RECHECK_INTERVAL` | `5m` |
  | `SB_SECRET_PROVIDER_REVOKE_AFTER` | `3` |
  | `SB_SECRET_VAULT_ADDR`, `_KEY_NAME`, `_TOKEN_FILE`, `_NAMESPACE`, `_CACERT` | empty |
  | `SB_SECRET_VAULT_TRANSIT_MOUNT` | `transit` |
  | `SB_SECRET_PKCS11_MODULE`, `_TOKEN_LABEL`, `_PIN_FILE`, `_KEY_LABEL`, `_DECRYPT_KEY_LABELS` | empty |
  | `SB_SECRET_PKCS11_GCM_IV` | `auto` |
  | `SB_SECRET_PKCS11_RUN_DIR` | `/run/sandboxd/pkcs11` |

- **Sandboxes lose access they had.** No sandbox reaches the cloud metadata service, and there is no setting to allow it. A program that used a service on its own server needs `SB_SANDBOX_NODE_PORTS_ALLOW`, unless it is the egress gateway, DNS, or ports 80 and 443 on a server that serves public URLs. Sandboxes that talked to each other on one server need `SB_SANDBOX_INTERCONNECT=true`. A program that listens only on `::1` no longer starts; one that listens on `[::]` still accepts IPv4. If you changed `SB_EGRESS_DNS_PORT` or `SB_EGRESS_PROXY_PORT` in `egress-gateway.env`, set them in `sandboxd.env` too.
- **New limits.** A container sandbox is stopped once it writes more than its disk size plus 5%. The default disk size is 10 GiB, so the default limit is 10.5 GiB. Raise `disk_gb` at create, or set `SB_DISK_LIMIT_CHECK_INTERVAL=0`. A sandbox that needs more than 4,096 processes needs a higher `SB_SANDBOX_PIDS_LIMIT`. A gVisor sandbox gets one process per MiB of memory.
- **Local installs.** On `install.sh --local` and any server with `SB_ENABLE_NETWORK_RULES=false`, a Docker or containerd create, start or update that asks for network policy gets `501`. A stopped sandbox with such a policy no longer starts there. `SB_ALLOW_UNENFORCED_NETWORK_POLICY=true` restores the old behavior for local development (not allowed in enterprise mode).
- **Firecracker templates.** Delete and re-create every Firecracker template. Rebuilding one is not enough, because a rebuild reuses the old disk. Until then, creates from it fail with `501`, and its warm-pool slots are released. A Firecracker sandbox stopped before the upgrade cannot start again: destroy it and create a new one. Upgrade `toolboxd` together with sandboxd (`SB_TOOLBOX_BINARY_PATH`). In a cluster, upgrade every Firecracker node before you re-create templates. A sandbox from a new template on an old node answers `503` to every call. A Firecracker create whose `env` has an empty key, a key with `=` or a NUL byte is now refused.
- **Docker-engine servers.** A create with network rules and no pool slot starts its own pause container. That adds about 100 ms at the median, and the server pulls `SB_DOCKER_NETNS_POOL_PAUSE_IMAGE` (`registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10`) when it starts. Point an air-gapped server at a mirror, or those creates fail. On a stock `docker0`, the bridge pool refuses the 1,001st running sandbox with `503`. `SB_DOCKER_BRIDGE_SLOTS=1023` gives back the 23 slots held in reserve on a server that never builds images.
- **Docker snapshots.** A sandbox created from a new Docker snapshot no longer inherits the source sandbox's `env`. Pass `env` at create, as containerd already requires. A snapshot saved by an older release can still hold the values: delete it and save it again.
- **E2B creates.** New E2B sandboxes get IDs from the keyed fingerprint, in the same `sb-<16 hex>` shape. Existing sandboxes keep theirs. For 4 minutes after an upgraded server starts, a retried E2B create still finds a claim made before the upgrade, so an in-flight retry still gets its sandbox.
- **`Idempotency-Key` on create is checked.** On `POST /v1/sandboxes` and the Daytona create, a retry that reuses a key with a different request (another image, `env` value or network policy, for example) gets `422 idempotency_key_reused`, with the key in the message and no `Retry-After`. Before, it got the first sandbox and the new request was dropped. The same request still replays. Sandboxes created before the upgrade, and creates on a server with no server key, replay unchecked, as before. None of the five SDKs sends this header, so only callers that set it themselves see the change.
- **Toolbox connections.** Every toolbox call opens its own connection, and a connection to a sandbox that stops answering ends after `SB_TOOLBOX_DEAD_PEER_TIMEOUT` (30 seconds). A sandbox that answers nothing for that long while it still exists, such as a VM paused that long, loses its open calls. Raise the setting, or set `0` and restart sandboxd.
- **Reconcile and audit.** A sandbox whose runtime cannot say whether it exists now stays as `error` until you destroy it, instead of being deleted. An address that keeps sending bad credentials adds up to one more `auth_denied` record per minute. In a cluster, SSH session records move to the sandbox's own server once every member runs v0.6.9.
- **SDKs 0.7.0.** The SDKs with the `Retry-After` change were published as 0.7.0 on 2026-11-02, to npm, PyPI, crates.io and GitHub Packages. The Go SDK comes with this tag. In Rust, `RetryConfig` gains a public field, `max_retry_after_ms`, so code that builds `RetryConfig` with a struct literal and no `..Default::default()` must add it.
- **Store schema.** One new table, `sandbox_create_digests`, is created automatically at start. Older releases ignore it. Nothing else in the database schema changes.
- **Re-run `install.sh`** to pick up the new watchdog. A binary-only upgrade keeps the old watchdog, which still works with the new daemon. On servers installed with `--ingress-proxy-routing`, re-run it to move the route resolver to the link address. New installs turn rpcbind off. Servers that already have it keep it as it is.
- **Terraform.** Set `admin_allowed_cidrs` (your office or VPN ranges) before the next `terraform plan`, or it fails. `0.0.0.0/0` also needs `allow_admin_from_anywhere = true`. The next apply sets the node metadata hop limit to 1.
- **Backups.** A backup made with an older `sandboxd-backup.sh` may not include the server key file, so it restores only onto the same machine. Update `sandboxd-backup.sh` and `sandboxd-restore.sh` from this release (the Ansible `configure-ops` playbook installs them), then take a new backup.
- **Rolling upgrades are safe.** Old and new servers work together in a cluster. Features that need every server, such as server-key rotation and the new SSH record placement, wait until every member runs v0.6.9.
- **Rolling back.** If you go back to v0.6.8, the firewall tables this release adds stay in place and only drop more traffic. Addresses blocked through the new `ip aerolvm_block` table stay blocked; once their sandboxes are re-created, run `nft delete table ip aerolvm_block`. The egress-gateway runbook has the steps. containerd network slots left in the new `releasing` state stay out of use until you free them by hand (#834 has the query).

name: v0.6.8: SSO, roles, and the caller in every audit record
body:
## Features in v0.6.8

Named callers, company SSO, roles, and the caller in every audit record. This closes the three questions a security review asks: can each person sign in with their company account, can access be limited by role, and is every action tied to a named person. It answers Discussions #646, #647 and #649 as one feature.

> **Identity is off by default.** With `SB_IDENTITY_ENABLED` unset, a server behaves exactly as before, except audit records now name `caller: operator` or `caller: system`. The operator token (PAT) is unchanged and stays the break-glass and node-to-node credential. Single-node and local Docker installs need nothing new.

### Highlights

- **Company SSO, with no login server.** People and CI sign in with your identity provider over OIDC; each node verifies the provider's signed token itself, so there is no session store and no new service to run. `aerolvm login --sso`, the dashboard, GitHub Actions and Kubernetes workload tokens all use it. Verified locally against Keycloak, with setup docs for Authentik and Zitadel; Okta, Entra ID and Google follow the same OIDC path.
- **Four roles, scoped to a team or the fleet.** `viewer`, `runner`, `auditor` and `admin`. Every route declares the permission it needs, and a team token sees only its own sandboxes.
- **Scoped API tokens for services and CI.** `avm_…` tokens are hashed, expiring and revocable within about 15 seconds across a cluster. Mint them with `aerolvm token create` or `POST /v1/tokens`.
- **The caller in every audit record.** A hash-chained `caller` field, plus a chain record for every create, delete, exec, file, port, snapshot and token call (kind `api`). A forwarded request is attributed on the owner node, with the edge node recorded as `via`.
- **Enforced SSO.** `SB_PAT_SCOPE=host` confines the shared operator token to the host and cluster peers, so remote people must use SSO or a scoped token.

---

### People and credentials

- SSO through OIDC, the Kubernetes way: the identity provider's signed token is checked on the receiving node and again on the owner node, with no trusted identity header. Issuers and role bindings live in `SB_IDENTITY_FILE` (strict YAML, reviewable, GitOps-friendly, reloaded on SIGHUP).
- `aerolvm login --sso` (browser) and `--device`; `aerolvm whoami` shows the bound principal, role and team.
- Google dashboard sign-in uses Google Identity Services, with no secret on the server.
- `avm_` tokens: SQLite on one node, Raft in a cluster. Default maximum lifetime 365 days (`SB_TOKEN_MAX_TTL`; 90 days in enterprise mode). A worker whose token mirror cannot sync for 60 seconds refuses `avm_` tokens with 503, while the PAT, OIDC and metrics keep working.
- The CLI warns before a token expires, and a 403 names the role that would allow the call.

### Roles and teams

- `viewer`, `runner`, `auditor`, `admin`; the `X-AerolVM-Team` header selects a team, and auditor and admin are fleet-wide.
- `aerolvm access review` produces SOC 2 access-review evidence from an S3 audit export.
- A Prometheus scrape needs only a `viewer` token (`metrics.read`), not an admin credential.

### Audit

- Every record gains a hash-chained `caller` and `request`; new record kinds `api`, `auth_denied` and `identity_config`.
- `SB_AUDIT_API_RECORDS` controls which calls are recorded (mutations by default); `SB_AUDIT_EXEC_COMMAND=full` also records `argv` (never env); `SB_AUDIT_API_DURABLE` fsyncs token and delete records (off by default, on in enterprise).

### Remote MCP OAuth

- Remote `/mcp` signs in with the company SSO (RFC 9728): the 401 names the resource metadata, a client discovers the issuer and gets an MCP-audience token, and the inner tool calls act only as that caller. The claude.ai connector is supported; ChatGPT is not claimed until a live check passes.

### Security

- WASM module references and catalogue delete are now gated on caller scope (#537, #777). A scoped tenant cannot resolve a module from a raw host path (an absolute path or `file://`) or delete a shared standard module; the reserved keywords, `oci://` refs and a tenant's own catalogue ids are unaffected. This was not reachable before this release, because scoped tenant tokens did not exist. Verified live on the single-node-wasm scenario.

### Upgrade notes

- **Nothing changes unless you set `SB_IDENTITY_ENABLED=true`.** The PAT is unchanged; audit records simply gain `caller: operator` or `caller: system`.
- **Rollback floor: do not roll back past v0.6.8 once a node has written a `caller` record.** An older binary fails strict audit-boot verification on that log. Recovery is to stay on v0.6.8 or boot once with `SB_SECRET_AUDIT_BOOT_VERIFY=warn`. Upgrade the `aerolvm` CLI first, because an older `aerolvm audit verify` fails the same way.
- **Rolling upgrades are safe.** In a cluster the new audit fields and record kinds are written only once every member runs this release (the gossip `fv` gate); until then records are written as before.
- **Enterprise mode now requires `SB_IDENTITY_ENABLED=true` and `SB_PAT_SCOPE=host`.**
- **`SB_PAT_SCOPE=host` moves remote PAT users to SSO or a scoped token.** The dashboard, remote `/mcp`, remote SDK scripts and the Prometheus scrape then need a named credential; set an optional `metrics_token` in `config/secrets.yml` for the scrape (leaving it unset keeps the PAT).
- **Re-run `install.sh`** to pick up the PROXY-protocol wrapper on the L4 fallback. A binary-only upgrade leaves it off, so nothing breaks.

name: v0.6.7: Enterprise mode with the free download
body:
## Features in v0.6.7

### Highlights

- **Enterprise mode works with the free download.** Set `SB_ENTERPRISE_MODE=true` and point the new `SB_AUDIT_WITNESS_*` settings at an S3 bucket with Object Lock. Each server then keeps the fingerprint of its audit log in that bucket, where the server cannot change or delete it. A server refuses to start on a bucket that would not protect what it stores, or when its local log disagrees with the bucket.
- **`aerolvm audit verify`.** An auditor checks a server's audit history from any machine, against the bucket and the exported audit records. The result is PASS, FAIL or INCOMPLETE (exit 0, 1 or 3) for a time window the auditor chooses with `--since`.
- **Terraform and Ansible set it up.** `audit_witness_enabled = true` creates the locked bucket and a node role that can write fingerprints but cannot delete them. Ansible and `install.sh` carry the settings.
- **Open shells and exec streams survive route changes.** A sandbox exposing a port no longer disconnects every open `aerolvm shell`, exec stream and session attach on that node.
- **Terraform cluster deploys on the default settings work again.** The release now ships `cluster-sign-node.sh`, which every seed node downloads.

---

### Audit witness (#710, plan #655)

- Fingerprints are stored as locked object versions under `<prefix>/node=<SB_NODE_ID>/day=<UTC date>/head.json`.
- At startup the server checks, within 30 seconds, that the bucket has versioning and an Object Lock default rule at least as long as `SB_SECRET_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`, that the node can list it, and that a test delete fails both with and without the governance bypass header. Each refusal names what to fix; the runbook has an entry for every one.
- The server reads the bucket before every write. A fingerprint it did not write increments `aerolvm_secret_audit_witness_foreign_head_total` and fires the `SandboxdAuditWitnessForeignHead` alert. `SandboxdAuditWitnessShipFailing` fires when writes keep failing. An unchanged fingerprint is written again once a day, so an idle server still shows up every day.
- If the local audit log is edited or deleted after its fingerprint was stored, the server refuses to start. For a deleted log, the refusal says to rebuild the node under a new `SB_NODE_ID`.
- What it does not prove: the newest 30 seconds, a server compromised from its first boot, or writes by another node that shares the node role (those are detected and alerted on, not prevented). The verifier, not the boot check, catches a server that rewrote its history and stored a matching new fingerprint.

### Fixes

- A cluster create naming a platform volume for the first time no longer fails with "sandbox not found", and a volume in use can no longer be deleted (#711).
- Caddy keeps an open WebSocket for up to 10 minutes after a configuration reload instead of closing it at once with code 1001 (#713). Long sessions still close 10 minutes after a reload.
- `cluster-sign-node.sh` is a release asset (#714). Releases v0.6.0 to v0.6.6 did not ship it, so the seed of a Terraform deploy on the default settings failed to download it.

### Upgrade notes

- **Nothing changes unless you set `SB_AUDIT_WITNESS_BACKEND`.** With it unset, no S3 request is made and boot is unchanged.
- **A witness needs a unique `SB_NODE_ID` on every node,** single servers included. The default `standalone` is refused. Rebuilding a node means a new id, because Object Lock keeps the old fingerprints.
- **Use a dedicated bucket with Object Lock enabled at creation,** in COMPLIANCE mode, with a default retention at least as long as `SB_SECRET_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`. Enterprise mode needs an `https` endpoint.
- **Keep audit exports for at least as long as the window you verify.**
- **Re-run `install.sh` to pick up the Caddy change.** Routes written by an older sandboxd get the 10-minute delay when sandboxd next writes them.

name: v0.6.6: Runloop SDK compatibility and aerolvm shell
body:
## Features in v0.6.6

### Highlights

- **Runloop SDK compatibility.** Code written against the official Runloop SDKs (`@runloop/api-client`, `runloop_api_client`) runs on AerolVM. Set `RUNLOOP_BASE_URL` to `https://<host>/runloop` and `RUNLOOP_API_KEY` to the same token the rest of the API uses. Devboxes, commands, files, and disk snapshots work. A retried request does its work once.
- **`aerolvm shell`.** Open an interactive shell in a sandbox, and come back to it after you disconnect. `aerolvm exec -it` works the way `docker exec -it` does.
- **A command is not run twice.** All five SDKs re-send an exec only when it never reached the server. A Rust command longer than 30 seconds is no longer cut off and sent again.
- **Docker 29, Firecracker DNS, and warm pools.** Container stop, crash, and remove events are read again, so a stopped sandbox no longer leaves its firewall rules for the next one. A Firecracker guest gets DNS, so hostname allowlists and name lookups work. Warm-pool sandboxes survive a stop and start, a snapshot, and a sandboxd restart.
- **A snapshot no longer replaces an image.** Saving a snapshot named `python` used to overwrite the `python` image on that node. Snapshots are now stored under a name the server chooses.

---

### Runloop facade (#641, #700)

- Devboxes: create (including `create_and_await_running`), get, list, update, suspend, resume, keep-alive, shutdown, and `wait_for_status`. Shutdown is terminal and stays answerable after the sandbox row is gone, including across a sandboxd restart.
- Commands: execute, async and sync execute, status, kill, and stdin. Named shells keep their working directory and environment. Output streams while the command runs. A command is remembered until 24 hours after it finishes, so a retry after a restart does not start a second run. If the facade cannot tell whether a command ran, the same `command_id` gets `409`.
- Files: read, write, upload, and download. Relative paths resolve against the devbox user's home directory.
- Disk snapshots: create, status, list, update, delete, and create a devbox from a snapshot. A snapshot belongs to the account that saved it. In a cluster, a devbox created from a snapshot runs on the node that holds it.
- `blueprint_id` / `blueprint_name` map to an image through `SB_RUNLOOP_BLUEPRINT_MAP_JSON`. An unmapped blueprint is refused. The default image is `ubuntu:22.04` unless that map says otherwise.
- Create fields with no equivalent are refused with `501` rather than ignored. Tunnels (`enable_tunnel`, `remove_tunnel`, PTY tunnels, and `tunnel` on create) answer `501`. Blueprint builds, storage objects, secrets, agents, axons, and network policies have no route. Devbox logs, usage, and SSH keys are routed and answer `501`. Eviction notices answer `404`.
- The listener accepts HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) next to HTTP/1.1, which is how the TypeScript SDK talks to a plain `http://` base URL.
- Docs: Use the Runloop SDK.

### CLI (#633)

- `aerolvm shell <sandbox>` reuses the newest running terminal session of that name, or starts a login shell. Detach with Ctrl-]. It refuses to run without a terminal, and it refuses WASM and isolate sandboxes.
- `exec` accepts `-it` / `-ti`, sends a `TERM` the image knows, and forwards window resizes.
- Help is grouped as "Work in a sandbox", "Manage sandboxes", and "Setup".

### SDKs (#643, #639)

- Exec (`POST .../toolbox/process/execute`) is re-sent only on connection refused, DNS failure, connect timeout, or HTTP 429/503. Every other call keeps the existing retry policy.
- The Rust client no longer applies a 30-second limit to the whole request. The 30-second limit is the connect timeout.
- `gpus` now reaches the server from TypeScript, Python, and Rust. `template_id` now reaches the server from TypeScript, Python, Rust, and Java. Java's `createWithImage` also sends `name`, `tags`, the egress fields, and `platformVolumes`.
- Python accepts `create(image=...)` and `Sandbox.exec("cmd")`. Rust `Sandbox::exec` accepts `&str` and `String`.
- The TypeScript publish job no longer logs in with a long-lived npm token. SDK package versions in this tag are 0.6.4.

### Runtime fixes (#638, #642)

- Docker 29 dropped `id` from container events. sandboxd reads the id from `Actor.ID`, so stop, crash, out-of-memory, and external remove events apply their firewall and lifecycle updates again.
- Firecracker guests get the host's resolvers in `/etc/resolv.conf`. containerd guests get the same treatment.
- A warm-pool sandbox that was stopped and started, snapshotted, or left running across a sandboxd restart is adopted again instead of answering 503 "sandbox not adopted". Restarting sandboxd no longer deletes live pool sandboxes.
- Destroying a sandbox no longer logs a bogus cluster warning once those Docker events flow.
- A Daytona session command that prints to stderr keeps that stderr. The result no longer depends on which pipe arrives first.

### Snapshots, builds, and auth (#672, #674, #675, #676)

- Each new snapshot is committed under its own local image tag. Snapshots saved before this release keep the image name they already have, and they keep working.
- Image cleanup no longer deletes a snapshot's image once nothing is running from it.
- Image builds from v1, snapshot registration, and Daytona go through one service path. A build made with an account token pulls every base image from the registry, so it cannot read another account's image off the server. A Dockerfile that names a snapshot or a built image is refused. Operator builds are unchanged.
- In a multi-tenant deployment, five requests that used to be allowed are now refused: `/debug/vars` and `/v1/metrics` require an operator credential, a user token with an empty account is refused, `X-Cluster-*` headers are dropped when cluster mode is off, and toolbox `/admin` paths are refused. The E2B envd access token is compared in constant time. On a single-operator install every caller is an operator, so owner scoping still limits no one.
- WASM file upload, download, and listing stay inside the sandbox work directory. A symlink that resolves outside it is refused. Container and Firecracker sandboxes serve files from inside the guest, so this does not apply to them.

### Facade and cluster correctness (#677–#695, #699)

- E2B and Runloop use the same error table as v1. Failures those SDKs should retry no longer come back as a flat 400.
- A Daytona or E2B create placed on another node arrives there with its request body. A v1 create resolves volume mounts before the replicated spec is promoted, so a failover recreate mounts the right thing.
- v1 and Daytona creates accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` header. A retry with the same key returns the first sandbox. Creates without the header are unchanged. E2B and Runloop keep their own idempotency.
- Daytona toolbox reads are bounded. Isolate exec is dispatched in the sandboxd process. A toolbox target is refused when the sandbox is not running.
- Tag edits and facade compatibility state are replicated, so they survive failover. Snapshot lists for Daytona and E2B are paged from the store.

### Dependencies

- Go: `golang.org/x/sys` 0.49.0, `github.com/aws/smithy-go` 1.28.4, `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/credentials` 1.20.8, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk` 1.47.0.
- Rust SDK: `rand` 0.10.3, `tokio` 1.53.2, `serde` 1.0.229.
- Docs: Starlight 0.42.6, `@astrojs/markdown-satteri` 0.4.3. GFM rendering uses the Sätteri processor.
- Actions: `download-artifact` 8.0.2, `upload-artifact` 7.0.2, `setup-node` 7.1.0, `attest-build-provenance` 4.2.2.

### Upgrade notes

- **Snapshots.** Snapshots saved before this release keep their old image names and keep working. A new snapshot is stored under a name the server chooses, so it cannot replace another image.
- **Account-token image builds.** They always pull base images from the registry. A Dockerfile that names a snapshot or a previously built image is refused. Builds made with the operator token are unchanged.
- **WASM files.** A path that resolves outside the sandbox work directory, including through a symlink, is refused.
- **Multi-tenant auth.** `/debug/vars` and `/v1/metrics` are operator-only. A user token with an empty account is refused. Toolbox `/admin` paths are refused. A single-operator install is unchanged in practice, because every caller there is an operator.
- **Create retries.** v1 and Daytona still create a second sandbox when a create is retried, unless the request carries an `Idempotency-Key` header.
- **SDKs.** The packages published as 0.6.4 on 2026-10-10 do not include the exec-retry and create-option fixes. Those fixes are in this tag's SDK source and reach the package registries with the next SDK publish.

name: v0.6.5: Agent CLI and MCP server, egress domain filtering
body:
## Features in v0.6.5

> **Installer fix: upgrade if you install with `install.sh`.** Starting 2026-10-09, Caddy's Cloudsmith apt repo refuses downloads, so a new node comes up with no Caddy and no HTTPS. `install.sh` now installs Caddy from Caddy's GitHub release, with a checksum check. It also removes the broken apt repo from hosts that an older installer set up, so re-running the installer on them works again. (#627)

### Highlights

- **`aerolvm`, a CLI for agents.** Agents can drive sandboxes from their own shell tool, with no MCP setup. Its binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows (amd64 and arm64) are attached to this release.
- **MCP server, local or remote.** `aerolvm mcp` serves sandbox tools over stdio. sandboxd can also serve them at `/mcp` (opt-in, `SB_MCP_ENABLED`).
- **Egress domain filtering.** Allowlist by hostname, change a sandbox's policy while it runs, and use named profiles, learn mode, method and path rules, TLS inspection, and credential injection. Hostname allowlists work on every runtime, Firecracker included. Method and path rules, TLS inspection and credential injection are not available on Firecracker or WASM yet.
- **Sandbox names are unique per owner**, and `GET /v1/sandboxes?name=` looks a sandbox up by name.

---

### Agent CLI and MCP server (#584–#589)

- **`aerolvm` CLI** commands: `create`, `list`, `get`, `exec`, `logs`, `cp`, `ls`, `expose`, `start`, `stop`, `destroy`, `snapshot`, `health`, `version`.
  - It never prompts. Data goes to stdout and everything else to stderr. Every command takes `--json`, and with it errors come back as structured JSON.
  - `exec` returns the command's exit code: 128+n for a signal, 124 on `--timeout`. Ctrl-C kills the remote command.
  - `create` is safe to retry, `destroy` succeeds when the sandbox is already gone, and repeating `expose` returns the same URL.
  - `cp` streams files in both directions.
  - Install just the CLI with `install.sh --cli-only`.
- **`aerolvm mcp`, the stdio MCP server.**
  - Tool groups: `core` (create, list, destroy, exec, read, write, list files, expose port), `files` (edit, search, grep) and `process` (start, logs, stop). `--read-only` leaves out every tool that changes something.
  - Pinned mode (`--sandbox`, optional `--create-if-missing`) binds the server to one sandbox. If that sandbox disappears, it is recreated and the result says so.
  - Cost guards are on by default: sandboxes it creates stop after 30 minutes idle and are destroyed after 24 hours, and an unpinned server creates at most 5 sandboxes.
  - `aerolvm mcp config <claude-code|claude-desktop|cursor|vscode>` prints the client setup without printing your token.
- **Remote MCP endpoint on sandboxd (`/mcp`).** Clients connect with a URL and an API token, with nothing to install.
  - **Off by default** (`SB_MCP_ENABLED`). It serves a pinned sandbox only.
  - Tool calls go through the regular API, so auth, owner scoping and cluster forwarding are unchanged.
  - Requests carrying an `Origin` header are refused unless the origin is listed in `SB_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. Each token is rate-limited (`SB_MCP_RATE_LIMIT`).
  - It ships with metrics, an SLO dashboard row, an alert and a runbook.
- **Distribution.** This release attaches the `aerolvm` binaries, covered by the checksums, SBOM and provenance like every other asset. The repo also includes a Claude Code plugin and an MCP Registry entry. npm and MCP Registry publishing stay off until they are enabled in the repo.
- Docs: new `cli` and `mcp` pages.

### Egress domain filtering (#622, #630)

- **Closes existing gaps.**
  - Non-privileged sandboxes no longer get `CAP_NET_RAW`, so they cannot send raw or spoofed packets.
  - Host input is guarded for block-all and allowlist sandboxes.
  - Egress rules are re-applied when a container is started outside sandboxd.
  - WASM `network_block_all` holds from the first connection.
- **Hostname allowlists** (`network_allow_out` accepts hostnames).
  - A new `sandboxd egress-gateway` process does filtering DNS plus a transparent SNI/Host proxy. `install.sh` installs it as the `aerolvm-egress-gateway` unit.
  - Every runtime uses the same matching rules.
  - Denials are explained and audited.
  - The operator file (`SB_EGRESS_OPERATOR_FILE`) sets the default policy, a ceiling, a deny floor, an internal zone and an upstream proxy.
- **Live policy.**
  - `PUT /v1/sandboxes/{id}/network/policy`, plus E2B's `updateNetwork`.
  - Named egress profiles, replicated through Raft.
  - Learn mode (`GET .../network/learned`).
  - A policy check endpoint, and `--allow-host` on the CLI and MCP server.
  - Supported in all five SDKs.
- **Rules.**
  - `network_egress_rules` match on HTTP method and path.
  - Optional TLS inspection with a per-node CA.
  - Credential injection: the sandbox holds a placeholder, and the gateway adds the real secret from the sandbox's sealed env.
  - Per-binary rules on runc.
  - Firecracker and WASM sandboxes refuse `network_egress_rules` for now.
- **Firecracker egress.** NAT, a firewall for each guest and strict `rp_filter` on the TAP subnet. Block-all, CIDR and hostname policies now work on microVMs.
- **Private-cloud TLS.** Custom-domain and wildcard certificates can come from an internal ACME CA (`SB_TLS_ACME_CA`, `SB_TLS_ACME_CA_ROOT`) or from Caddy's internal CA (`SB_TLS_ISSUER=internal`).
- Fixes from the coverage follow-up (#630):
  - A failed egress gateway now exits and gets restarted, instead of running while serving nothing.
  - The DNS rate limiter no longer lets one in 256 new sandboxes burst past its limit.
- Docs: Egress Domain Filtering, Egress Profiles and Learn Mode, Egress Rules and Inspection, and an egress-gateway runbook.

### Sandbox names and lookup (#580, #581)

- Sandbox names are unique **per owner**, not per install. One tenant's name no longer blocks another tenant, and a conflict no longer reveals that the name exists.
  - The store index is migrated in place at startup.
  - Cluster name keys stay compatible during a rolling upgrade.
- `GET /v1/sandboxes?name=<name>` returns zero or one of the caller's sandboxes. In cluster mode it goes straight to the owning node instead of querying every node.
- SDKs:
  - TypeScript, Python, Rust and Java gain `name` and `tags` on create, plus `getByName` / `get_by_name` / `GetByName`.
  - Go SDK errors are now typed `*APIError` values, and `ErrNotFound`, `ErrConflict` and `ErrNameLookupUnsupported` work with `errors.Is`.

### Exec, files and listing (#582, #583, #624)

- **Exec streams stop their command when the client disconnects.** toolboxd kills the whole process group. Streams send a ping every 30 seconds, so proxies that close idle connections don't cut off a long, quiet command. Sessions are unchanged.
- **Login shells keep the image's `PATH`.** Tools an image adds (for example `go` or `cargo`) are found again through exec, E2B commands, Daytona sessions and terminals.
- **Streamed file transfers.** The Go SDK adds `DownloadFileStream` and `UploadFileStream`. toolboxd and the WASM toolhost stream downloads instead of reading the whole file into memory.
- **Single-node list paging.** `GET /v1/sandboxes` accepts `limit` and `page_token`. Paging applies only when the caller sends one of them, so older SDKs still get the full list.

### Reliability fixes

- **Reconcile no longer destroys sandboxes mid-create.** The orphan sweep and the zombie-route sweep both skip creates that are still in progress. (#626)
- **Ingress:**
  - Preview URLs no longer return 404 to clients that connected before their route existed: the catch-all closes the connection so the client reconnects.
  - Caddy admin writes are serialized, which fixes the `EOF` errors and lost layer-4 routes.
  - Reconcile re-adds routes missing from Caddy. (#595)
- **Cluster:**
  - A failed cross-node create releases its name right away instead of holding it until the reservation expires. (#594)
  - Fixed a placement-subscriber data race. (#592)
  - Running sandboxes can reclaim capacity held by parked warm-pool slots, so nodes no longer sit at "cpu reservation exceeded" with real resources free. (#600)
  - containerd sends the cluster token when pulling a snapshot that lives on another node. (#593)
  - js-bundle uploads and deletes appear in the cluster list immediately. (#599)

### Security and dependencies

- Patched `http-cache-semantics` for GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp. (#577, #579)
- Closed the five open Dependabot alerts in the docs site and the pinned npm CLI. (#631)
- Bumped containerd to 2.4.1 and the AWS SDK S3 client to 1.114.0, among other dependency updates. (#601–#617)
- Go line coverage is now 97%, and the races the coverage suite found are fixed. (#618, #619)

### Upgrade notes

- **Sandbox names:** a name that starts with `owner:` or looks like a generated ID (`sb-` followed by 16 hex characters) is now rejected at create with a 400.
- **Raw sockets:** non-privileged sandboxes no longer have `CAP_NET_RAW`.
- **Hostname egress** (`SB_EGRESS_FQDN_ENABLED`) is on by default. It does nothing until a sandbox uses a hostname. Container runtimes need the `aerolvm-egress-gateway` unit, which `install.sh` installs; without it, hostname creates return 501.
- **Remote MCP** (`SB_MCP_ENABLED`) is off by default.
- **SDKs:** this release does not change SDK package versions. The SDK changes listed above reach the package registries with the next SDK publish.

name: v0.6.3: Security release, host escape and path traversal
body:
## Features in v0.6.3

Security release. The issues below were found in a review of the sandbox control plane. No configuration change is required to pick up the fixes.

### Highlights

- **Mount sources can no longer run a command on the host.** An option-shaped external-storage mount source was parsed as a flag by the host mount tool and could run as the daemon user (GHSA-5pqm-4fh4-585q). Those sources are now rejected.
- **WASM toolhost no longer executes on the host.** `/process/exec/stream` and `/process/code-run` spawned a host shell or interpreter. Both fail closed with 501. `POST /process/execute` still runs inside the WASM engine.
- **Path checks on sandbox IDs, bundle digests, and WASM module refs.** A `..` id, digest, or relative module ref can no longer escape its directory.
- **Signed releases.** Each release publishes an SLSA provenance asset. Go fuzz targets cover the untrusted-input validators.

---

### Security

- **Mount source (critical, GHSA-5pqm-4fh4-585q).** Mount sources are rejected when they are option-shaped or contain control characters. Every mount adapter ends its options with `--` before the source and target.
- **Sandbox ID (high, #532).** A caller-influenced id, including one carried on the cluster create-forward header, was used as a host path. Ids are now checked (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}`) at create and again at use.
- **WASM toolhost (critical, #534).** The two host-backed routes are removed. Restoring a confined streaming or code-run path is left for a later release.
- **js-bundle digests (high, #540).** A digest is accepted only when it is 64 hex characters, before any filesystem access.
- **WASM module refs (high, #542).** A relative ref is confined to the modules directory. Absolute paths stay the operator escape hatch.
- **containerd build contexts (#549).** Extraction stops at 100,000 entries and 2 GiB of regular-file bytes, so a context tar cannot fill the disk.
- Rust `anyhow`, `h2`, and `rustls` are past the published advisories. Vulnerable copies bundled in the pinned npm CLI are replaced. The uncalled `x/crypto` openpgp advisory is ignored on purpose.

### Supply chain (#531, #545, #546, #550)

- OpenSSF Scorecard workflow and badge. `SECURITY.md` is the disclosure policy.
- SLSA build provenance is a release asset.
- Workflow pip and npm installs are pinned by hash.
- Native fuzz targets run on the untrusted-input validators.
- CodeQL findings from this pass are cleared. The Codacy scan is removed.

### Fixes

- **SSHFS mounts (#529).** The adapter used `-o foreground`, which sshfs 3.x rejects, so those mounts never came up. It now uses `-f`. The same change adds the integration tests that refuse an option-shaped mount source.
- **macOS install.** `install.sh` no longer exits silently while detecting `PUBLIC_HOST`. (#527)
- **TypeScript SDK publish** uses npm OIDC. (#528)

### Upgrade notes

- WASM `/process/exec/stream` and `/process/code-run` return 501.
- Sandbox ids outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}` are rejected at create.

- `SB_DOCKER_TOOLBOX_LOOPBACK` is **off by default**. Linux and every existing deployment are unchanged. Each Docker sandbox publishes only its toolbox port, bound to `127.0.0.1`, and dockerd assigns the host port.

### Other

- The cluster replica-budget test no longer flakes. (#525)
- The npm publish workflow and the TypeScript package repository fields match the repo. (#526)

### Upgrade notes

- Re-run `install.sh --local` on a Mac that failed the earlier installer. Set `SB_DOCKER_TOOLBOX_LOOPBACK` only for that rootless macOS layout.
